title: Trash Ingredients That Are Actually Worth Money
briefSource: Notion: Carousel Scripts - Posts 9-16 + Origin Story
editorialNotes: "$3-4 of flavor" per rind is script copy with no cited source: body copy only, never hero type.

thread.element: ingredient moving from a trash can to a plate

copy.headline: You're throwing away ingredients worth more than what you cooked.
Parmesan rinds →
items: Drop it into soups, stews, or risotto while it simmers.
It melts into the broth and adds depth you can't get from anything else.

copy.headline: Pasta water →
items: That starchy water is a free emulsifier. A ladle of it turns any sauce silky.
Every Italian restaurant does this. Every home cook pours it down the drain.

copy.headline: Chickpea can liquid (aquafaba) →
items: The liquid in your can of chickpeas whips like egg whites.
Meringue, mousse, cocktail foam — all from something you were about to rinse off.

copy.headline: Bacon grease →
copy.body: Strain it into a jar. Store in the fridge. Use it instead of butter or oil for roasting vegetables, frying eggs, or making cornbread. Your grandparents did this. It's not gross. It's free cooking fat.
